title: Quantum Cooling by Classical Shadows
abstract: Cooling to ground states of many-body Hamiltonians by imaginary-time evolution is central to quantum simulation, but its non-unitary aspect prevents direct implementation on a quantum computer. Existing routes restore it by importing structure from outside the intrinsic quantum dynamics, e.g. by parameter estimation on many copies or recursive compilation. Here, we show that a single randomized snapshot of the quantum many-body system is sufficient to steer the state along the cooling direction on average. Our algorithm, shadow chain, uses randomized measurements to collapse the state to its classical record, which fixes the next unitary update. Snapshots across steps form a trajectory that is a quantum-executable sample of an auxiliary-field path integral; fluctuations among trajectories are exponentially suppressed in system size. With the randomness supplied intrinsically by the Born measurement rule, the trajectories sample themselves rather than going through external accept-reject steps. The resulting algorithm is ansatz-free and exact upon extrapolation to the continuous limit, with the exponential cost confined only to system size rather than temperature.

title: Gapless Nature of Spin Liquid in the $S=1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet with Neural-Network Quantum States
abstract: Whether the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet hosts a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ or a gapless $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid remains a central open question in frustrated magnetism. Here, we address this question by directly computing the triplet gap with a neural-network quantum state that does not presuppose any specific spin-liquid structure. Applying a time-reversal symmetric transformer-based ansatz to clusters of up to $768$ sites, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies on two-dimensional lattices with periodic boundary conditions and estimate an energy per site of $-0.43873(12)$ in the thermodynamic limit. Finite-size scaling of the magnetic order parameter and triplet excitation gap shows that both extrapolate to zero in the thermodynamic limit. Together, these results provide independent and direct evidence of a gapless spin-liquid ground state, consistent with the $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid. More broadly, they demonstrate that neural-network quantum states can resolve ground-state properties of frustrated quantum magnets that remain challenging for conventional numerical methods.

title: Measurement of Magnonic Quantum Geometry
abstract: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in macroscopic quantum phenomena, including quantum Hall effects and flat-band superconductivity. However, since quantum geometry is encoded in wavefunctions rather than energy spectra, direct experimental characterization remains a formidable challenge. This challenge is particularly acute for quasiparticles in quantum materials, whose wavefunctions are generally inferred from effective low-energy models rather than measured directly. Here, we establish an experimental framework for characterizing the quantum geometry of magnons, a ubiquitous Bosonic quasiparticle of magnetically ordered states. We show that the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) cross-section measures geometric parameters of the spinor wavefunctions of ferromagnets. By tracking the energy- and momentum-dependent INS intensity, we extract the quantum geometric tensor without requiring detailed knowledge of microscopic spin-spin interactions. Our results establish magnons as an ideal arena for experimentally probing quantum geometry and open new avenues for exploring geometry-driven magnon transport and quantum Fisher information in magnetic materials.

title: From RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ to Ideal Geometry: Parallel-Face Octahedra for Kitaev-Dominated Interactions
abstract: RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ has recently been identified as a Kitaev spin liquid candidate via neutron scattering. To assess its proximity to the Kitaev limit, we perform \textit{ab initio} calculations of magnetic interactions, finding good agreement for the Kitaev and off-diagonal exchanges, while the Heisenberg exchange is ferromagnetic rather than the experimentally fitted antiferromagnetic one. We also identify a sizable antiferromagnetic out-of-plane exchange not captured in previous analyses. Extending the study to eight substitutional analogs in the $MT_3Q$O$_{11}$ family ($M$ = Ru, Os; $T$ = P, As; $Q$= Si, Ge), we observe strong variations in magnetic interactions, highlighting the tunability of this materials class. Finally, inspired by RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$, which exhibits a near parallel-face octahedral arrangement, we compare idealized geometries and show that the parallel-face configuration yields a Kitaev-dominated regime, suggesting a new structural route to the Kitaev limit.

title: Finite-time quenches across first-, second-, and infinite-order transitions in XXZ spin chains
abstract: We investigate how equilibrium quantum phase transitions manifest themselves in small systems driven out of equilibrium by quantum quenches. We consider linear ramps of the anisotropy in spin-1/2 and spin-1 XXZ chains, which host transitions of first, second, and infinite (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, BKT) order. We consider system sizes available in current quantum simulators and investigate how the order of the transition, the symmetries, and the ramp duration affect the decomposition of the time-evolved state into the instantaneous eigenbasis. The order of the transition determines the dynamics: across the BKT transition, moderately slow ramps already keep the system close to its ground state, corresponding to an adiabatic evolution, whereas for the second-order Haldane-N\'eel transition a ramp roughly three times slower is required to reach the same regime. Across the first-order transition, since the dynamics conserves the magnetization of the initial state, we observe the formation of ferromagnetic domains, separated by a single domain wall for slow ramps and by multiple walls for faster ones. Interestingly, shortly after the transition, the state evolves as a coherent beating between domain-wall states, a behavior captured by the recently proposed quantum-state texture.

title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
abstract: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.

title: Optical response of quantum metals
abstract: Strongly interacting quantum systems display puzzling electrical transport properties whose interpretation remains controversial. Many theoretical and phenomenological analyses assume that the complex behaviour observed in such `quantum materials' originates either from quasi-particles dressed with an anomalous electron self-energy or from collective excitations associated with hydrodynamic flow. Despite their distinctly different starting points, the underlying assumption is that dissipation of electrical current arises from the relaxation of the total momentum of charge carriers. This classical description breaks down in the absence of long-lived charge carriers. In such strange metals dissipation seems to be governed by the rate at which equilibrium is thermally restored, and it has been suggested that this constitutes an upper bound, known as the `Planckian limit'. Here we show that in this quantum regime a description of the conductivity in terms of relaxation rates no longer suffices: strange metal transport is carried instead by fast-decaying current fluctuations, which together with quantum detailed balance give rise to the widely observed Planckian dissipation. The distinction between classical and quantum metals becomes transparent when experimental data is analysed in terms of the current-current correlation function instead of the optical conductivity. When applied to the cuprate superconductors, such analysis uncovers that the strange metal response is present at all doping levels, and that a second, classical component develops above optimal doping. This simple, but powerful, approach further highlights essential features associated with superconductivity, (pseudo-)gaps, provides fresh insight in the properties of metals, and identifies key areas where progress in our theoretical understanding is needed.

title: Fragmentation in Non-Hermitian Many-Body Systems
abstract: In non-Hermitian (NH) fermionic chains with spatially random imaginary gauge fields, single-particle eigenstates exhibit erratic NH skin localization with strongly fluctuating, subexponential decay, distinct from both conventional skin accumulation and Anderson localization. At finite filling, Pauli exclusion suppresses macroscopic accumulation and instead leads to fragmentation of the particle density, in sharp contrast to Hermitian disordered systems. Using exact free-fermion methods, we show that the density organizes into disconnected regions of high and low occupancy, forming spatially separated Fermi domains whose number $N_{\mathrm{FS}}$ scales subextensively with system size $L$. Remarkably, fragmentation is not only an equilibrium property but also emerges dynamically in the NH evolution, unlike in Hermitian systems where such structures are not dynamically selected. This behavior admits a Coulomb-gas description in a stochastic potential, establishing a direct link between erratic NH skin localization and real-space fragmentation of many-body states.

title: Chiral Majorana Charge Kondo Criticality
abstract: Unambiguous identification of chiral Majorana edge modes remains challenging because the transport signatures proposed for them can also arise from conventional mechanisms. Here we identify the chiral Majorana charge Kondo (CMCK) critical point as a more discriminating many-body route to detect chiral Majorana edge modes. This criticality arises in a charged island hosting a single chiral Majorana edge mode, where Majorana self-conjugacy locks normal and anomalous tunneling amplitudes, so that each physical lead provides two Kondo screening channels without fine tuning. Ordinary subgap states generically break this locking and drive the system toward conventional charge Kondo (CK) behavior. In the simplest two-terminal geometry, CMCK and conventional CK share the critical conductance $G^*=e^2/2h$, but their leading conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/3}$ and $T$, respectively. Their residual entropies also differ, as do the crossover exponents under gate detuning and contact asymmetry. For $N$ leads, CMCK conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/(N+1)}$, and for $N\geq3$ even the critical conductance differs from that of conventional CK with the same number of leads. These universal signatures are testable using established charge-Kondo measurement techniques.

title: Charge-Transfer Energy Governed by $f$-$d$ Coulomb Interaction in Rare-Earth Systems
abstract: The $f$-$d$ Coulomb interaction ($U_{\rm fd}$) plays a central role in low-energy theories describing valence fluctuations and quantum valence criticality in rare-earth systems. In contrast, core-level spectroscopies have conventionally been analyzed using the phenomenological charge-transfer energy ($\Delta$), and the relationship between these two descriptions has remained unclear. Here, we develop a spectroscopic framework demonstrating that the charge-transfer energy contains an $f$-$d$ Coulomb contribution $U_{\rm fd}n_d$ arising from the $d$-electron occupation ($n_d$), leading to the charge-transfer energy $\Delta'$. We apply this framework to the prototypical valence-transition compound YbInCu$_4$ and demonstrate, from combined analyses of core-level photoemission and $L$-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy, that the observed spectroscopic evolution across the first-order valence transition is consistently interpreted in terms of the variation of $\Delta'$.

title: Compact Projected Pfaffian States for Rydberg-Blockaded Quantum Spin Systems
abstract: We numerically demonstrate that a compact projected Pfaffian ansatz effectively describes the ground state of the nonintegrable PXP model. The variational wave function is obtained by applying separate Gutzwiller and Rydberg-blockade projectors to a general fermionic paired state, and each blockade-allowed configuration has an amplitude given by the Pfaffian of a configuration-selected pairing matrix. The exact blockade-projected product state of a known frustration-free deformation of the PXP model lies within the variational manifold and provides a physically motivated initial state for the variational Monte Carlo optimization toward the ground state of the pure PXP model. For a one-dimensional system of $N$ sites, optimizing all symmetry-allowed pairings in an $O(N)$-parameter wave function yields a near-exact ground state with a normalized energy variance (V-score) of order $10^{-9}$ despite the exponentially large blockade-constrained Hilbert space. On the square lattice, an $O(N)$-parameter wave function with the same amplitude structure yields relative energy errors below $0.2\%$ for clusters accessible to exact diagonalization and produces magnetizations consistent with available benchmarks. These results show that the same projected Pfaffian construction can be applied to blockade-constrained systems in both one and two dimensions.

title: Exact environment checkpointing for memory-limited DMRG and TDVP
abstract: Finite matrix-product-state sweep algorithms, such as the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP), store one environment tensor per site. At the bond dimensions needed for frustrated and two-dimensional systems this stack, rather than the state itself, exhausts the memory of the device. We adapt checkpointing to these sweeps: every $k$-th environment is kept, with $k\approx\sqrt{N}$ for $N$ sites, and the blocks in between are rebuilt when the sweep returns to them. The rebuild repeats the original contractions, so energies and states are reproduced bit for bit when the contractions are deterministic. Environment memory falls by 4.6-10x on cylinders of 96-384 sites. Bond-dimension searches with an implementation that rebuilds checkpoints at each half-sweep give gains of 1.77 for one level and 2.07 for two levels with eight contraction chunks on a single 141 GB GPU, using a 144-site triangular $J_1$-$J_2$ cylinder and stored baselines with matching chunking. Separate timings with checkpoints retained across half-sweeps give a one-level overhead of 6-15%, depending on the local eigensolver. At $D=1536$ the two-level schedule with eight chunks takes 1.42 times the sweep time of the equally chunked stored baseline, or 1.79 times that of the unchunked stored baseline. Simple models of the memory and the run time reproduce the measurements to within a few per cent. Unlike offloading, the method needs no host memory or disk, and the two can be combined. Implementations are provided for ITensorMPS.jl, TeNPy, MPSKit.jl and quimb.

title: Spectroscopic evidence for unconventional surface magnetism in the Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$
abstract: Kondo insulators have a non-magnetic bulk due to many-body screening of local moment by conduction electrons. However, the surface of these systems has reduced density of itinerant electrons and may experience a Kondo breakdown, leading to recovery of non-zero local moments and possible magnetic order. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the (010) surface of a $d$-$p$ electron Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$, which is predicted to host a bulk $d$-wave altermagnetic state in the absence of Kondo screening. We find anisotropic splitting on the surface states with a maximum in the $k_z$ direction and a minimum in the $k_x$ direction. The splitting is apparently suppressed with increasing temperature or with Te doping, suggesting that the splitting arises from a magnetic order rather than Rashba effects. Considering the proximity of the bulk to a $d$-wave altermagnetic state and considering the symmetry of the crystal on the surface, we postulate that our observations may be consistent with an emergent surface altermagnetic order. Such an unconventional 2-dimensional magnetic order naturally hosted on an insulating, non-magnet bulk substrate may offer a promising platform for versatile applications.
authors: Erin E. Fleck Jonathan A. Sobota

title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
abstract: At strong on-site repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto configurations without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments, for few fermions in the square-lattice Hubbard model and, where the arguments allow, on any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on any $N\geq2$-site graph, $\mu_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$, for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $\mu_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count, as four hops permute particles by at most a transposition or 3-cycle; for uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$ the slope is $\alpha(N,n)=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$, fixed by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles. (3) At large finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient, an exact trace checked by exact diagonalization, is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Under a Peierls flux, the exchange slope $\alpha(N,2,\Phi)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cos\Phi_\square$ ($L\times L$ tori, $L=3$ or $L\geq5$) carries the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, while the doublon (bound-pair) hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $\pi$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows numerically, up to $O((2\lambda)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the permutation bound, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moment structure and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

title: Angular dependence of the low-temperature skyrmion state in Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$
abstract: In the cubic chiral magnet Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$, a low-temperature skyrmion state (LTS) and a metastable tilted conical state emerge for magnetic field along $\langle 100\rangle$, both stabilized by magnetocrystalline anisotropies. We report how these states evolve when the magnetic field is rotated from $\langle 100\rangle$ via $\langle 111\rangle$ to $\langle 110\rangle$. Measurements of the magnetization and the AC susceptibility are combined with broadband microwave spectroscopy on the same cuboid sample at 5\,K. In the microwave spectra, the characteristic gigahertz excitations, notably the counterclockwise gyration mode of the skyrmions, provide a direct indicator of the character of the magnetic states and a qualitative measure of their volume fractions. Both techniques consistently show that signatures of the LTS decrease in strength under rotation and are observed only for field directions within ${\sim}20^{\circ}$ of $\langle 100\rangle$. In this range, the field values at which the skyrmions unwind remain essentially unchanged. In contrast, signatures of the tilted conical state persist up to ${\sim}40^{\circ}$, beyond which the conventional sequence of helical, conical, and field-polarized states is recovered. Thus, the tilted conical state, while being a prerequisite for the nucleation of the LTS under field sweeps, is not sufficient for its formation.

title: Two channels of magnetic renormalization in the terahertz lattice response of FePS$_{3}$
abstract: Interlayer vibrations probe how magnetic van der Waals layers are stacked and coupled. In the zigzag antiferromagnet FePS$_3$, ultrafast experiments show that the interlayer shear couples strongly to the magnetic order, but not how magnetism renormalizes the shear stiffness and damping. Here, using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we measure the anisotropic conductivity of FePS$_3$ from 1.6 to 300 K and in fields up to 7 T normal to the layers. We observe absorption bands at 0.6-0.8 and 1.3-2.4 THz that persist into the paramagnetic phase. The lower one is consistent with an interlayer shear resonance; the magnetic order stiffens one of its in-plane components and softens the other, reversing their splitting at the N\'eel temperature. We identify two channels of magnetic renormalization: frequency shifts are confined to the ordered phase, whereas the linewidths of this resonance and most oscillator strengths follow short-range spin correlations persisting well above the transition. The field acts mainly on the higher resonance in one orientation: near 3.2 T, its softening accelerates and its linewidth has a cusp-like minimum, consistent with critical slowing down of a field-induced order parameter. These results give an equilibrium view of spin-shear coupling, which is anisotropic and persists above the N\'eel temperature through short-range correlations.

title: Multi-symmetry projected coupled cluster theory with triples corrections
abstract: Symmetry projection and coupled cluster theory provide complementary descriptions of static and dynamic correlation. We introduce two approximate perturbative triples corrections to spin- and point-group-projected coupled cluster with single and double excitations (PCCSD). The coherent $(T)$ correction combines triples intermediates over the projection grid, whereas $+(T)$ evaluates the conventional triples expression using PCCSD amplitudes. Both recover conventional $(T)$ in the absence of projection. We assess these corrections for N$_2$ and C$_2$ dissociation, $3d$ transition-metal monoxides, and Cr$_2$. Projection improves the singles-and-doubles description and distinguishes selected low-lying symmetry sectors. For the six-monoxide benchmark subset, coherent $(T)$ reduces the PCCSD mean absolute error from $13.4$ to $3.0~\mEh$, achieving accuracy comparable to conventional CCSD(T). Both triples corrections restore the short-bond minimum missing from the PCCSD curves of Cr$_2$, with coherent $(T)$ giving a well depth closer to extrapolated DMRG. In contrast, $+(T)$ provides more balanced N$_2$ and C$_2$ dissociation curves. These results demonstrate the benefits of perturbative triples in PCC, while their system-dependent performance highlights the need for a more systematic treatment.

title: Self-doped correlated adatom lattices on cubic boron nitride
abstract: We survey triangular adatom lattices on the (111) surfaces of cubic boron nitride (cBN) for strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems. Using density functional theory combined with the constrained random phase approximation and charge self-consistent dynamical mean-field theory, we identify twelve promising candidates. Group-III (group-V) adatoms on the N- (B-)termination realize clean one-band Hubbard systems, while group-III and transition-metal (V, Cr, Mn) adatoms on the B-termination realize two-band Hubbard systems. Importantly, the polar III-V character of cBN induces self-doping by $\pm 1/4$ electron away from integer filling. With strong Hubbard (and Hund's) interactions and small hoppings, most systems are doped Mott insulators. Heavy quasielectrons with mass renormalizations up to 4 and strong local moments up to 2.5 $\mu_B$ put our systems into a regime where unconventional superconductivity on the triangular lattice has been predicted.

title: Role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in noncentrosymmetric tetragonal magnets
abstract: We investigate the role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in stabilizing square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in a noncentrosymmetric localized-moment model on a square lattice. The magnetic phases are determined using self-consistent mean-field calculations. We first consider a single crystal-field doublet with exchange and polar-type Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. We find square skyrmion lattices with distinct magnetic periods, as well as a rectangular skyrmion lattice that spontaneously breaks the in-plane fourfold rotational symmetry. Their stability and field-induced phase sequences are strongly controlled by the crystal-field wave function, including reentrant behavior of the rectangular phase. Second-neighbor exchange further modifies the competition among these states. When a second crystal-field doublet is retained, additional rectangular skyrmion lattices with distinct modulation patterns emerge, together with axial single-$Q$ states and various double-$Q$ states. These results demonstrate that crystal-field degrees of freedom provide a microscopic mechanism for tuning the stability, spatial symmetry, and topology of multiple-$Q$ magnetic states.

title: Excitonic magnetism and competing valence bond solid instabilities in $d^4$ ruthenium compounds
abstract: Spin-orbit entangled $d^4$ Mott insulators serve as a rich playground for unconventional magnetism and competing quantum electronic ground states. Intra-ionic spin-orbit coupling $\lambda_{\rm{SOC}}$ generates a non-magnetic $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ singlet ground state separated from an excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. The effective intra-atomic gap ${\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$ between the ground state and lowest excited state is determined by $\lambda_{\rm{SOC}}$ and non-cubic crystal field ${\Delta}_{\rm{cf}}$. The intersite magnetic exchange $J_{\rm{ex}}$ induces dispersion of the excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. When the triplet bandwidth $W_{\rm{t}}$ overcomes ${\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$, the system undergoes long-range magnetic ordering which is viewed as a condensation of spin-orbit excitons and called excitonic magnetism. In this review, we systematically survey representative $d^4$ ruthenium compounds across four distinct structural connectivities of Ru-ligand octahedra, from K$_2$RuCl$_6$ with isolated octahedra, corner-sharing perovskite Ca$_2$RuO$_4$, edge-sharing honeycombs, to corner-sharing pyrochlores, and map them onto a conceptual parameter axis of $W_{\rm{t}} / {\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$. We demonstrate that $d^4$ ruthenium compounds not only represent evolution from a $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ Mott state to excitonic magnetism but encompass a broader competition of diverse electronic phases arising from spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, electron hopping, crystal field and bond covalency inhabiting similar energy scales. Near excitonic quantum critical point, where $W_{\rm{t}} \sim {\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$, lattice geometry and chemical bonds of constituent atoms play a decisive role in selecting the electronic ground state, frequently driving valence bond solid formation that pre-empts excitonic quantum criticality.

title: Unconventional Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect beyond Magnetization Scaling Driven by Pulse-Field-Induced Metamagnetism in Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
abstract: First-order phase transitions often proceed through metastable states and complicated phase coexistence, yet such nonequilibrium processes are obscured in bulk measurements. The magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) probes the local off-diagonal optical response, offering access to local magnetic dynamics beyond bulk measurements. Here, we investigate the magnetic-field-induced antiferromagnetic (AFM)-ferrimagnetic (FRM) transition in the polar insulator Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ using pulsed-field MOKE measurements extended for the first time up to 60 T and down to 1.4 K. The MOKE response exhibits unexpected and huge nonmonotonic transient behavior across the metamagnetic phase transition. The MOKE behavior does not show any scaling with the bulk magnetization, pointing to an MOKE analogue of the unconventional anomalous Hall effect. This is a new class of off-diagonal response emerging exclusively at the boundary between competing magnetic orders. At low temperatures, MOKE profiles are highly reproducible in detail, whereas at elevated temperatures they depend strongly on magnetic-field history and pulse protocol, suggesting changes in the driving mechanism of the phase transition. We infer that the excess MOKE anomaly originates from AFM-FRM phase interfaces in real space. Our results, extending MOKE into the 60 T regime, establish pulsed-field magneto-optics as a novel probe capable of uncovering transient and hidden field-induced phenomena through unconventional off-diagonal optical responses.

title: Hund physics in the quarter-filled two-band Hubbard-Kanamori model: Crystal-field splitting and non-local Correlations
abstract: We address the effect of crystal-field splitting and non-local correlations in the quarter-filled two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model. The role of the Hund's coupling in this configuration is not obvious since the atomic ground state has only one electron per site. Yet, previous works identified fingerprints of the Hund's coupling defining a weak Hund's metal at least at finite temperature. Using single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) and two-site cellular DMFT based on a selected configuration-interaction solver we investigate the zero-temperature properties of the weak Hund's metal. Within DMFT we draw the boundary for the weak Hund's metal, which is consistent with previous finite-temperature results. Interestingly, we find that the fingerprints of the Hund's coupling are quite robust to the lifting of the orbital degeneracy and they survive up to splittings of a quarter of the bandwidth, well beyond those at which a two-stage Kondo screening disappears. Including non-local correlations in cluster DMFT demonstrates the robustness of the single-site DMFT picture, even if Mott localization occurs at smaller interactions. In the metal the intersite correlations are weak and insensitive to $J$, while in the localized state we find nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic, antiferro-orbital correlations that are manifest also in the mutual information between sites.

title: Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
abstract: Layered palladates provide a $4d$ platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO$_2$, RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$, La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$, and La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-$d_{z^2}$ orbital. LaPdO$_2$ and BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$ and quadlayer La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-$d_{z^2}$ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

title: Self-attention is a Dyson equation for many-body machine learning
abstract: Why does symmetric sum-pooling (DeepSets) predict ground-state potentials to sub-meV accuracy, yet fail for correlated wavefunctions and excited states? Sum-pooling is a mean-field (Hartree) model: its $O(1/N)$ off-diagonal Jacobian suffices for nearsighted ground-state energies, but erases nonlocal two-body correlations. We show that self-attention is a real-space Dyson iteration whose Boltzmann (softmax) kernel acts as a two-body self-energy. Because physical Hamiltonians act pairwise, L\"owdin's 2-RDM theorem and the Galitskii--Migdal relation guarantee that iterating a two-body propagator captures the full energetics of correlated matter. When fitting a fractal backflow determinant, DeepSets blurs the nodal surface onto a mean-field envelope, whereas self-attention recovers the fractal attractor. Seen through this lens, the unreasonable effectiveness of attention is not an accident; in a universe built from pairwise interactions, two-body attention is all you need.

title: Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$
abstract: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$, as a spin-$2$ hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe$^{2+}$ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at $T_{\rm N}\approx9.8$\~K, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd$_3$Ga$_5$O$_{12}$. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

title: Random matrix discrepancy -- CLuP algorithm and parametric RDT approach
abstract: We study information-theoretic and algorithmic aspects of random matrix discrepancy in proportional regime. The problem amounts to finding $\kappa=\min_{\x\in\mB^n}\|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bar{A}_i\x_i\|_2$, where $\bar{A}_i\in\mR^{d\times d}$ is a collection of $n$ iid GOE matrices, $\mB^n$ are vertices of the unit cube in $\mR^n$, and $\alpha=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\frac{n}{d^2}$ is a proportionality constant. Strong progress is made in several directions: (i) We develop a Random duality theory (RDT) framework and utilize its a lifted variant to establish lower bounds on $\kappa$, which precisely match the bounds obtained via the first moment in [81]. (ii) To address analytical challenges, we propose a negative Hopfield model as a proxy for implementation of a fully lifted RDT. On the 2nd lifting level, this model fits remarkably well between the information-theoretic lower bounds from [81] and the algorithmic upper bounds from [38]. (iii) On the 3rd and 4th lifting levels, parametric RDT concepts predict a sizeable computational gap for lower $\kappa$ values in the proxy model. Extending proxy information-theoretic fitting to algorithmic suggests a similar computational gap for matrix discrepancy in low $\kappa$ regime, aligning with [73]. (iv) We design a Controlled Loosening Up (CLuP) algorithm for matrix discrepancy. Its performance strongly matches our analytical results -- closely approaching information-theoretic predictions in lower $\alpha$ ranges (indicating a small or nonexistent computational gap) and following the proxy model's algorithmic predictions in higher $\alpha$ ranges (indicating a sizeable computational gap). Both the information-theoretic and algorithmic predictions match the corresponding phenomenologies of the symmetric binary perceptron (SBP) vector analogue in the entire $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$ range [1,2,14,31,51,92,111].

title: Exact mobility edges in high-dimensional quasiperiodic networks
abstract: Inspired by the one-dimensional hidden self-duality [Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 246301 (2025)], we establish a generalized theoretical framework for a specific class of high-dimensional quasiperiodic network models. Specifically, as long as the periodic network acts as bond-decorating links and the quasiperiodic potentials are spatially separable, the system can be mapped onto an effective high-dimensional generalized Aubry-Andr\'e equation by integrating out the periodic sites. This mapping restores the hidden self-duality symmetry in these complex models, thereby yielding exact mobility edges. Taking two-dimensional and three-dimensional models as examples, we demonstrate the consistency between the theoretical prediction and the numerical results. This paper establishes a clear paradigm for mapping high-dimensional quasiperiodic networks to high-dimensional Aubry-Andr\'e models, providing a systematic pathway for the construction and exploration of the exact mobility edge in high-dimensional systems.

title: Velocity weakening and stick-slip in mean-field depinning with stress overshoots
abstract: We study a fully connected depinning model with transient stress overshoots of strength $M$, driven through a spring of stiffness $k_0$. Combining exact stationary relations, linear stability analysis, direct simulations, and population dynamics, we connect the force--velocity characteristic to stick-slip motion and quasistatic avalanche statistics. For $M>1$, two distinct stiffness scales organize the response. At $k_0=k_{\rm w}\equiv M-1$, the stationary characteristic first develops a velocity-weakening branch, whereas $k_0=k_{\rm q}\equiv(M-1)^2/(4M)$ marks the onset of finite-amplitude stick-slip in the quasistatic limit. Their separation produces an intermediate regime in which the quasistatic force converges to a stationary value, whereas finite-velocity driving produces stick-slip below a critical velocity. Quasistatic avalanches in this regime undergo transient amplification and display an excess of large, asymmetric events---"ghost kings"---that remain finite. By contrast, at and below $k_{\rm q}$ the same amplification produces system-spanning "genuine kings" and a finite quasistatic force cycle. These results show how elastic loading dynamically selects among the branches of a reentrant force--velocity relation and clarify the connection between velocity weakening, stick-slip, and runaway avalanches.

title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
abstract: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze. We introduce a local disordered spin-1 chain in which a single domain wall explores an exact binary tree of configurations. Random fields create strongly correlated disorder on this tree, as in generic interacting systems, while the absence of loops keeps the problem tractable. We rigorously bound the spreading of the domain wall at strong disorder, and efficient numerics on exponentially large trees indicate a localization transition at finite disorder strength.

title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
abstract: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity. The resulting equations naturally decompose into contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher order paths through the network. We leverage this decomposition to express the effective monosynaptic connection between two neurons in terms of experimentally measurable statistics of the activity, and in particular, their high-frequency correlations. In this way, we show that it is possible to recover network connectivity from neural activity.

title: Magnon binding in a quantum Hall ferromagnet with a periodic electric field
abstract: A spin wave in a filling-one quantum Hall ferromagnet is neutral but carries an electric dipole perpendicular to its momentum. A spatially periodic electrostatic potential therefore creates parallel channels for spin waves. We use this established mechanism to calculate how confinement changes the exchange binding of magnons travelling in the same direction. Narrower channels increase the overlap of their transverse wavefunctions and strengthen the effective attraction. In an isolated harmonic channel, the energy required to remove one magnon from a cluster of $N$ is $\pi(k_*\ell)^4N(N-1)/4$ times the transverse level spacing to leading order, where $k_*$ is the mean wave number along the channel and $\ell$ is the magnetic length. We predict the frequency and momentum dependence of the spectral line for adding a second magnon to one already present, both in an isolated channel and in a coupled array. Tunnelling in a wide array can make the binding energy exponentially small, while a strip narrower than the transverse pair size recovers one-dimensional binding at sufficiently weak attraction. We also find that a moving potential can carry a single wave packet with less spreading than free propagation when its initial group velocity matches the potential's speed.

title: Thermal-energy relaxation in chiral quantum Hall edge mode
abstract: We study the nonequilibrium state generated by a real Ohmic contact (ROC) in the charge-fractionalization regime. We then investigate its thermal-energy relaxation along a quantum Hall edge mediated by a fictitious Ohmic contact (FOC) with large capacitance and perfect coupling to the edge. For cold Ohmic contacts, the electron distribution function and current noise are fully described by their equilibrium forms and the corresponding Fermi-Dirac distribution. In contrast, in the case of hot Ohmic contacts, strong thermalization effects do not drive the outgoing state into complete equilibrium. Both the distribution function and the noise retain signatures of the initial nonequilibrium state and therefore cannot be characterized solely by the effective contact temperature, contrary to common assumptions.

title: Strain-Engineering Giant Pseudo-Electric Fields in Multilayer Graphene
abstract: Electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials can be engineered in solids through lattice distortions, providing a versatile means of tuning electronic band structures. The pseudovector component, which generates pseudo-magnetic fields, has received much attention for its ability to realize a zero-field quantum Hall effect. However, the pseudoscalar component, giving rise to pseudo-electric fields to which many electronic systems are intrinsically susceptible, has not yet been experimentally explored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence and profound consequences of the pseudoscalar potential in a multilayer graphene system. Atomic relaxation reconstructs the system into large Bernalstacked domains separated by one-dimensional rhombohedral channels. Within this inter-dimensional system, we achieve the first direct atomic-scale imaging of distinct lattice deformations in graphene under strain. In rhombohedral channels, we observe that the tensile lattice deformation induces giant pseudo-electric fields, producing ultra-flat dispersion with divergent density of states and a large energy gap. This results in enhanced electronic correlations, leading to flat-band instabilities and striped modulation in the density of states that would otherwise require strong external displacement fields. Moreover, the gap opened by the pseudoscalar potential protects topological boundary states that persist in the absence of applied fields. Our results provide a comprehensive atomic-scale characterization of graphene elasticity and direct spectroscopic evidence for the nontrivial pseudo-electric field arising from lattice distortion. More broadly, it provides an intrinsic and tunable pathway to new quantum states

title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
abstract: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schr\"{o}dinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. A comparison of our results with data from other publicly available three-body codes as well as with the energies of well-known atomic counterparts, in particular, with vibrational energy levels of the molecular hydrogen ion, shows a good agreement and confirms the accuracy of the numerical data. We found that GEM significantly improves the precision of the obtained trion energies compared to previous calculations. Our calculations demonstrate that, for most semiconductor compounds, only one trion state with zero total angular momentum exists.

title: Flat-band driven bipolar anomalous Nernst effect towards volt-scale transverse thermoelectric conversion
abstract: Unipolar anomalous Nernst thermopiles are critically plagued by metallic interconnects, which induce heavy Joule dissipation and compromise the module's packing density, ultimately capping voltage generation. Here, we circumvent these limitations by establishing an intrinsic bipolar anomalous Nernst effect (BANE) paradigm, enabling seamless series integration analogous to Seebeck n-p pairs without passive metallic bridges. Focusing on flat-band topological systems, through machine learning assisted screening across multiple target properties, we identified 249 BANE materials, exhibiting near-room-temperature polarity switching. Guided by this predictive framework, we experimentally realized this phenomenon in single crystals of the Weyl ferromagnet, Co$_2$TiGe. Strikingly, while its intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) remains rigorously temperature-invariant up to the Curie temperature, the anomalous Nernst signal undergoes a sharp polarity inversion across $T \approx 225$ K. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to the interplay between flat bands and Weyl nodes, where thermal depopulation shifts the chemical potential across the band edge, inverting the sign of $\partial \sigma_{xy} / \partial \epsilon$ via the Mott relation. This work opens an avenue toward compact, monolithic transverse thermopiles capable of volt-scale generation free from interfacial parasitic dissipation.

title: Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
abstract: Materials informatics increasingly targets multicomponent materials, yet experimental datasets inevitably contain non-ideal variations arising from imperfect uniformity and reproducibility in composition, coating formation, and measurement. Whether machine-learning prediction accuracy scales with amount of data under these conditions remains unclear. Here, we develop an automated platform that produced and optically characterized 11,520 radiative-cooling coatings spanning nine material and processing parameters. Forward and inverse neural networks, and a spectrum-conditioned diffusion model were trained on subsets of 10 to 10,000 samples. All models exhibited power-law scaling, with prediction errors decreasing with dataset size. Experimental inverse-design validation showed that larger datasets produced spectra closer to a broadband-emitter target. The diffusion model generated multiple candidate parameter sets, allowing selection among alternative solutions based on ease of fabrication, cost, and scalability. These results demonstrate predictable learning-curve scaling in non-ideal experimental data and provide a quantitative basis for estimating the benefit of additional experimental data, and thus the cost-effectiveness of materials-informatics.

title: IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation
abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

title: Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
abstract: Magnetic d-electron oxides usually have a long-range-ordered ground state and an above-ground-state disordered para phase. The historical Slater-Mott controversy still reverberating to date pertains to understanding the origin of the insulating vs metallic nature of these two phases. Slater suggested that the insulating character evolved from the long-range order (LRO) antiferromagnetic (AFM) cell-doubling, leading to energy band repulsion and thus to forming a band gap. The reliance on LRO to explain gapping suggests that the absence of LRO in the spin-disordered para-phase would deprive the system from band repulsion, thus predicting a metallic paramagnetic (PM) phase. This, however, conflicts with numerous current observations. The alternative Mott-Peierls-Hubbard view abandons the mean-field-like band structure view emphasizing instead the local interelectronic repulsion U as a strong correlation signature of gapping both at the presence or absence of LRO. However, U is not an easily measured or calculated quantity in periodic systems, a situation often leading in practice to treating U as an adjustable parameter. The current work uses a parameter-free mean-field-like approach (Density Functional Theory, DFT), allowing energy-lowering symmetry breaking. This is done by considering local magnetic motifs as building blocks of the macroscopic AFM or PM phases. It is found that even when such motifs are isolated electronically from each other (i.e. vanishing LRO) by embedding them in quantum barriers (such as magnetic NiO6 octahedra surrounded locally by wide-gap MgO) they exhibit an intrinsic band gap. Thus, the origin of the band gaps in AFM or PM phases need not be LRO or strong correlation and can be understood within the mean-field-like band structure approach with symmetry breaking.

title: Robust Antiferromagnetic Ordering above 500 K in a Family of Bilayer van der Waals Materials
abstract: Stabilizing magnetic order above room temperature in layered materials is highly desirable for low-dimensional spintronics applications. However, realizing room-temperature antiferromagnetism in layered magnets remains challenging. Here, we present a layered semiconducting oxyhalide material family, Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$ ($X$ = F, Cl, Br), which exhibits robust high-temperature antiferromagnetic ordering. The two-dimensional nature and scalability of this system are demonstrated by atomically resolving the van der Waals gap of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Br$_2$ and synthesizing centimeter-scale single crystals of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$. Temperature-dependent neutron scattering and magnetization measurements determine their G-type magnetic structure and transition temperature. Remarkably, the N\'eel temperature of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$F$_2$ ($\sim$580 K) is the highest among all reported layered antiferromagnets. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that strong nearest-neighbor superexchange interactions along both out-of-plane and in-plane directions, particularly the magnetic couplings along lattice $c$ direction within the bilayer motif, are primarily responsible for the high N\'eel temperatures in Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$. In contrast, inter-bilayer spin couplings are negligibly weak, without much influence on the stabilization of the antiferromagnetic order. Therefore, theoretical calculations predict that this robust antiferromagnetic order could persist or even strengthens at room-temperature even at the monolayer limit. Our results highlight iron-based layered oxyhalides as a promising platform for exploring beyond-room-temperature antiferromagnetism in the two-dimensional limit, holding immense potential in areas like information storage and spin-based devices.

title: Machine Learning the $GW$ Self-Energy Operator for Real Materials
abstract: Machine learning of $GW$ in solids has largely focused on prediction of scalar quasiparticle energy corrections. Here, we introduce a phase-aware many-body transformer that predicts the full $\mathbf{k}$-resolved complex self-energy matrix. As a proof of principle, we apply the model to predict quasiparticle energies before and after diagonalization of the quasiparticle Hamiltonian, obtaining a test set mean absolute error (MAE) of 29 meV for a dataset of 1745 2D materials in the static COHSEX approximation and 60 meV for a more limited dataset of 433 materials calculated within a plasmon-pole model. COHSEX pretraining followed by finetuning reduces this MAE to 42 meV. The predicted matrices also accurately reproduce QP wavefunctions.

title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the $\Gamma$ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. We further show that external vertical electric fields, twist engineering, and both out-of-plane and in-plane strain provide efficient means to tune the band alignment, charge transfer, and Rashba parameters. In particular, electric fields and mechanical strain can drive reversible transitions between type-II and type-III band alignments while simultaneously modifying the Rashba spin texture and the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) window. The twisted heterostructure with $\theta = 21.79^\circ$ exhibits similar tunability, including strain-induced transitions between distinct band-alignment regimes. These findings establish MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs as versatile multifunctional platforms combining electrically tunable Rashba spin splitting with controllable type-II/type-III band alignment, offering promising opportunities for next-generation TFETs and spintronic devices.

title: Scaling a Universal Graph Neural Network Force Field to Billions of Atoms on Desk-Side GPUs
abstract: Machine-learning force fields are capable of simulating billions of atoms, but usually require high-performance supercomputing clusters. We show that a universal graph neural network force field, ALIGNN-FF, evaluates energies and forces of more than one billion atoms on desk-side computers such as the NVIDIA GB10, which has 128 GB of unified memory, by using a cube-and-halo decomposition. The halo contains every atom within the model's 20 {\AA} receptive field, which makes the result exact. One GB10 holds 216,000 atoms with forces as a single graph. The cube-and-halo decomposition removes this limit, enabling an evaluation of 2 billion atoms on nine GB10s. We also demonstrate three case studies: a billion-atom polycrystal, a 102-million-atom microelectronic gate stack and a 1.07-million-atom satellite tobacco mosaic virus in water. This brings single-point evaluations at experimentally relevant sizes within reach of one research group. The code is available at: https://github.com/atomgptlab/scalingmat.

title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Dissociative water adsorption is a key step in heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis, but on finite Ni nanosystems the OH$^*$ and H$^*$ fragments can occupy many combinations of surface sites, making exhaustive density functional theory (DFT) screening impractical. We introduce a graph neural network (GNN) framework with an adsorbate-free representation: candidate O- and H-binding sites are defined by sets of Ni atoms (\textit{anchors}), and each site pair is encoded as a graph constructed solely from these anchors and their local Ni environment. Using only MACE-relaxed bare Ni geometries as input, separate GNNs predict the DFT-reference adsorption energies of OH$^*$+H$^*$ configurations and whether the proposed binding sites would be retained upon DFT relaxation, eliminating the need to construct or relax adsorbates during screening. Trained across Ni nanoclusters and Ni(111)/Ni(100) surfaces, the energy model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.031 eV on the internal validation set and demonstrates transferability to unseen Ni$_{55}$, Ni$_{91}$, and Ni$_{130}$ clusters and larger surface cells, particularly for relative-energy ranking, although quantitative accuracy varies across systems. These independent tests also support the retention classifier's use as a conservative filter for selecting configurations likely to preserve their proposed binding sites. Application to Ni nanoparticles containing up to $\sim$3000 atoms identifies favorable co-adsorption motifs and shows that lower O-site coordination generally stabilizes the dissociated state, whereas H-site coordination has a weaker influence. The framework thus offers an efficient route to screening adsorption energetics, with potential extensions to other metals and adsorbate combinations.

title: Detecting False Self-Consistency in Density-Functional Calculations
abstract: Density-functional calculations feed materials databases and machine-learning models, and are declared converged when energy changes and residuals fall below thresholds. We show that these criteria, and even the agreement of independent optimizers, can accept a state from which the energy still descends or whose Hamiltonian is inconsistent with the energy. A variational formulation of self-consistency in the space of Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians yields a descent probe that exposes lower states accessible from a returned solution, and a frozen-orbital Janak test detects such an inconsistency. Both apply to any code without modification. In VASP, a UO$_2$ PBE+$U$ calculation converges 1.46 eV above a lower state, and CoO and FeO converge as metals 0.8-0.9 eV above insulating states. In a census of 339 converged calculations on tungsten-free Materials Project structures, recomputed with a modified static protocol, 57 (16.8%) show energy decreases above the threshold, 49 without an initial energy rise exceeding the tolerance.

title: Multiple moir\'e polarization textures in twisted trilayers
abstract: Twisted van der Waals layers exhibit nontrivial polarization textures from moir\'e-modulated stacking and the inherited sliding ferroelectricity. However, in any twisted bilayer, the topology of polarization texture is essentially fixed due to the inherent twist-stacking landscape for a given material. Here, this constraint is overcome in some twisted trilayers, where the relative moir\'e phase emerges as an additional structural degree of freedom. Using CrI$_3$ and BN as representative sliding ferroelectrics with distinct symmetries, it is clarified how the relative moir\'e phases reshape the trilayer stacking landscapes and tune the net polarization texture by layer sliding. The multiple moir\'e polarization textures can be attributed to the interference of original moir\'e patterns of the two bilayer subsystems.

title: Bias Conditioning and Long-Range Electrostatics for Consistent Machine-Learning Potentials of Electrified Interfaces
abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) of electrified interfaces need the bias as input, but it is unclear whether a scalar electrode charge suffices and whether short-range models capture the non-local response. We add charge and field conditioning to short- and long-range MLIPs. State-of-the-art field-conditioned short-range models overpolarize thick water films nearly twofold and miss work-function shifts at stepped Pt. Our long-range model captures both, needs only the electrode charge at metals as input, and reproduces ab initio simulations of the Pt(111)--water interface.

title: Large-scale Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations with Atomic Cluster Expansion potentials in LAMMPS
abstract: Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics (MCMD) simulations are widely used to study the properties of materials at the mesoscale. Simulations with hundreds of thousands of atoms usually rely on empirical potentials because MCMD with machine-learning interatomic potentials is impractical at this scale in existing implementations. Here, we introduce a hybrid MPI/OpenMP scheme for MCMD with Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) potentials in LAMMPS. Monte Carlo moves are evaluated from local energy changes and carried out in parallel over MPI ranks, while molecular dynamics is parallelized over OpenMP threads. At a fixed number of CPUs, the wall time of the Monte Carlo moves decreases by a factor equal to the number of MPI ranks. Larger simulation cells also reduce the statistical errors of free energy calculations because thermal fluctuations decrease with system size. We demonstrate the scheme by calculating free energies of the HCP and BCC phases in the strongly anharmonic Hf--Ti system and by simulating zirconium segregation in a nanocrystalline copper sample of 670,000 atoms. For Cu--Zr, an ACE potential and an empirical potential predict similar grain boundary compositions but different amounts of zirconium dissolved in the grains. The scheme makes MCMD simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials practical at the length scales of microstructure.

title: Moir\'e Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
abstract: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moir\'e Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling {\nu}_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moir\'e Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
abstract: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

title: High Characteristic Voltage YBCO Josephson Junctions Written With a Focused Helium Ion Beam
abstract: We report in-plane Josephson junctions written directly into YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-\delta}$ (YBCO) thin films with a focused helium ion beam (He FIB). The characteristic voltage $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of these junctions, where $I_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the Josephson critical current and $R$ is the junction resistance, sets the operating frequency and the sensitivity of the circuits built from them. A single line irradiation with a dose of \SI{500}{ions/nm} across a \SI{4}{\micro\metre} wide electrode produced a junction with $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of 929 \si{\micro\volt} at \SI{1.6}{K}, which is `higher than the 200 to 400 \si{\micro\volt} typical of junctions fabricated previously in our laboratory. Temperature dependent resistance, current-voltage characteristics, magnetic field modulation of the critical current, and Shapiro steps under 20.5~GHz microwave irradiation show Josephson behavior with an excess current below 5 percent of the critical current. The critical current falls steeply with temperature near the junction transition and saturates at low temperature. We attribute this behavior to a barrier at the metal insulator transition, where hopping conduction through localized states is active at finite temperature and freezes out on cooling. We describe the changes in surface preparation, sample selection, beam focusing, and sample storage that accompanied the improvement, although the present data do not separate their individual contributions. Larger characteristic voltages at these dimensions are an encouraging result for rapid single flux quantum and adiabatic quantum flux parametron logic and for superconducting quantum interference devices operating at elevated temperature.

title: Stabilization of LaH$_{10}$ with Thorium: Superconductivity in (La,Th)H$_{10}$ up to 232 K near 1 Mbar
abstract: Ternary lanthanum-based hydrides are among the best high-temperature superconductors. Here we show that substituting La with thorium stabilizes La(Th)H$_{10}$ clathrate structure at $\sim$1 Mbar while only minimally suppressing superconductivity. The resulting cubic (La,Th)H$_{10}$ phase, synthesized from relatively air-stable La$_2$Th, La$_3$Th and La$_5$Th alloys, reaches an onset $\textit{T$_c$}$ = 232 K at 134 GPa, as confirmed by contact resistance measurements. Superconductivity was verified by two independent methods: electrical resistance and contactless radio-frequency measurements under applied magnetic fields at various pressures. Using a record-high pulsed current of 380 mA, we investigated critical phenomena in P6$_3$/mmc-(La,Th)H$_9$ at 173 GPa, which allowed for the experimental determination of a single superconducting gap within the s-wave model: $\Delta(0) = 37 \pm 4.5$ meV and $2\Delta(0)/kT_c = 4.9 \pm 0.6$. The La-Th-H system is chemically rich: in addition to the decahydride and nonahydride mentioned above, we also identified nanocrystalline I4/mmm-(La,Th)H$_4$ (5-6 nm grain size), (La,Th)H$_6$, as well as $hP13$, $cF80$ and $A15$ phases with compositions of (La,Th)H$_{5.75-6.25}$ and $\textit{T$_c$}$ $\approx$ 83 K at 70-80 GPa, and a possible (La,Th)H$_{16}$ polyhydride.

title: Phase diagram and lattice structure of interlayer vortices in multilayer Ising superconductors in parallel magnetic fields
abstract: In this work, we investigate layered $s$-wave Ising superconductors under an in-plane magnetic field using self-consistent solutions of the microscopic Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations. Comparing bilayer, four-layer, and infinite-layer systems, we determine how the phase diagram and vortex structure evolve with layer number. Compared to standard Ginzburg-Landau treatments, our approach applies over a broader parameter regime and self-consistently resolves the spatial and layer dependence of the gap amplitude without prescribing its form. We find that the field range supporting the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) phase (defined as having no interlayer vortices) is reduced with increasing layer number and is essentially absent at nonzero magnetic flux in the infinite-layer system, consistent with recent thickness-dependent experiments on multilayer 2H-NbSe$_2$. In the infinite-layer limit, the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) phase containing interlayer vortices persists to progressively larger in-plane fields as temperature is lowered below the zero-field critical temperature, consistent with the experimentally observed low-temperature enhancement of the upper critical field. The vortex structure also evolves with interlayer hopping: in four-layer systems, for the fluxes and system sizes considered, increasing hopping reorganizes vortices from outer to inner interlayer junctions. At larger hopping, the gap distortion associated with an interior vortex extends to the surface layers, producing gap suppression comparable to that in the interior layers. Representative six-layer calculations show that interior vortices likewise produce a finite, although weaker, modulation of the surface-layer gap. These results highlight layer number and interlayer tunneling as key parameters governing the phase diagram and vortex arrangement in multilayer Ising superconductors.

title: Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures
abstract: In Eliashberg theory of phonon-mediated superconductivity with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential, the critical temperature $T_c$ marks the linear instability of the normal state. Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan (KAY) characterized it through the top eigenvalue of a compact operator on Matsubara-frequency sequences. They proved that $T_c$ is unique at strong coupling and conjectured $T_c<C(\lambda\langle\omega^2\rangle)^{1/2}$ for every coupling $\lambda$, with $\langle\omega^2\rangle$ the second moment of the normalized phonon spectrum and $C\approx0.1827$ sharp, a bound Leavens stated in 1977 on partly numerical grounds. A preprint by Kondratev, not yet peer reviewed, gives a proof of this bound and of all-coupling uniqueness. We give an independent proof, for every spectrum with finite second moment, based on a comparison principle that is also Kondratev's central step and was proved to first order by Bergmann and Rainer: strengthening the pairing interaction at every Matsubara transfer, strictly at the smallest one, strictly raises the top eigenvalue. At fixed $\lambda$ and $\langle\omega^2\rangle$ a single Einstein mode maximizes $T_c$. Convexity of the top eigenvalue in the spectrum gives sharp bounds on $T_c$ by the moments $\int\omega^n\alpha^2F d\omega$, $0\le n\le1$, including Leavens's zeroth-moment bound $T_c\le c_0\int\alpha^2F d\omega$, $c_0\approx0.231$ numerically, optimal at moderate coupling. All bounds persist under a Coulomb pseudopotential with symmetric cutoff. A prefix decomposition of non-increasing vectors proves a third KAY conjecture, not treated in the preprint. The finite-dimensional core, including that conjecture, is formalized in Lean 4, and two computer-assisted proofs independent of the comparison principle confirm the Einstein bound.

title: Inversion of magnetization anisotropy in low magnetic fields for textured Bi2223 superconductor due to magnetic responses from superconducting crystallites and intercrystalline boundaries
abstract: A detailed study of the magnetic anisotropy of a bulk textured high-temperature superconductor Bi2223 has been carried out. In the range of moderate and high fields (up to 1 kOe), the difference {\Delta}M between the upper and lower branches of the magnetization hysteresis loop is larger when the external magnetic field H is parallel to the normal of the texturing plane (H||NTP) than when H is parallel to the texturing plane (H {\perp} NTP). This magnetic anisotropy is typical for such textured superconductors. However, at small values of the maximum applied field Hmax (up to 15 Oe at a temperature T = 78 K), an anomalous inversion of anisotropy has been found: {\Delta}M(H||NTP) < {\Delta}M(H {\perp} NTP). It has been established that in the field range up to ~30 Oe (the first penetration field into Bi2223 crystallites is about 30 Oe at T = 78 K), the magnetic hysteresis is determined only by the magnetic flux trapped in the intercrystallite boundary subsystem. The pronounced platelet shape of the Bi2223 crystallites leads to partial screening of the external field inside the sample when the field is oriented parallel to the crystallite c-axis. The observed inverse anisotropy {\Delta}M(H||NTP) < {\Delta}M(H {\perp} NTP) has been explained by the fact that the effective magnetic field into the intercrystallite boundaries is smaller for the H||NTP orientation than for H {\perp} NTP. Therefore, when the field is oriented H||NTP, a larger external field is required for magnetic flux to penetrate into the sample inner than for the H {\perp} NTP orientation.

title: Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_{7-\delta}$
abstract: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}$) up to 96 K has been observed in the $\mathrm{La}_{2-x}\mathrm{Sm}_{1+x}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{Sm}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$ single crystal with $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}=92.5$ K under pressure. Within the Ullah--Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{MF}}$. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

title: Spontaneous Chiral Superradiance of a Spin-1 Condensate in a Ring Cavity
